# The Keeper of Unsent Things

Marrow Point Light stood at the end of a spit of black rock, where the sea had been taking bites out of the land for ten thousand years and had never once been satisfied. Tobias Wren came to it in the autumn of his fifty-second year, carrying one trunk, a barometer that had belonged to his father, and a silence he had been cultivating since his wife died.

The Lighthouse Board had sent him because nobody else would go. The previous keeper, a man named Harkness, had left in the spring without notice. His boots were by the door and his coat was on its hook. A skiff was missing from the boathouse, and it was found three weeks later on the mainland shore, tidy and empty. The Board wrote *departed* in its ledger and advertised the post.

Tobias did not mind the loneliness. He had come to believe loneliness was only a room, and that a man could furnish it.
